case_name: Surat Singh and Another v State of Punjab
respondent:
State of Punjab
Supreme Court of India

13 August 1976
Cr.A. No. 130 of 1972.
The Judgment was delivered by: UNTWALIA, J.
1. facts: This is an appeal u/s.2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970, by two persons who have been convicted by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana under Section 302, read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code, after setting aside their acquittal recorded by the trial Court.
Each has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life.
In the month of February, 1969 there was an election held for electing members to the Punjab Legislative Assembly.
From the constituency of the appellants and the deceased there were three contesting candidates in the field, namely : Pritam Singh, Joginder Singh and Gurmit Singh.
The first two were contesting the election as independent candidates and Gurmit Singh was an Akali candidate.
Shingara Singh, father of appellant Chain Singh, was helping Pritam Singh in the election while Khazan Singh, the deceased, who was killed in the occurrence, was on the side of Joginder Singh.
But according to the prosecution case the family of Shingara Singh continued to bear a grudge against Khazan Singh.
On February 28, 1969 at about 8.00 p.m. Shingara Singh, Chain Singh and Surat Singh are said to have gone in front of the house of Khazan Singh in village Dhalwali Dhab.
Shingara Singh raised a Lalkara and instigated Chain Singh to kill Khazan Singh.
Thereupon, Chain Singh is said to have given a spear blow on the left side of the chest of Khazan Singh.
On receiving that blow he fell down.
Appellant Surat Singh then gave two takwa (hatchet) blows on the left arm of Khazan Singh, causing simple injuries.
All the three were put up on trial for causing the murder of Khazan Singh.
The trial Judge acquitted them on appeal, the High Court giving benefit of doubt to Shingara Singh maintained his acquittal but convicted and sentenced the two appellants as stated above.
issues: Whether the judgment of the High Court is right in reversing the order of acquittal recorded in favour of the appellants by the trial Court.
Whether the dying declaration, Exhibit P-2, is a genuine and truthful statement of Khazan Singh.

Whether the evidence of the three eyewitnesses PW 3 Smt. Palo, wife of Khazan Singh, PW 4 Smt. Jogindro, daughter of Khazan Singh, and PW 5 Piara Singh, who is also a relation of Khazan Singh, can be relied upon.
Whether the High Court was justified in convicting the two appellants under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code with the aid of S.34.
petitioner_arguments: The appellant's counsel very strongly attacked the veracity and genuineness of Exh. P-16.
He said this could never be the version of Khazan Singh.
If that be so, counsel submitted that no reliance could be placed on the first dying declaration, Exh. P-2.
respondent_arguments: The High Court has rested the conviction of the two appellants chiefly on the dying declaration, Exhibit P-2 and the evidence of the three eyewitnesses PW 3 Smt. Palo, wife of Khazan Singh, PW 4 Smt. Jogindro, daughter of Khazan Singh, and PW 5 Piara Singh, who is also a relation of Khazan Singh.
court_reasoning: We are of the opinion that Exh. P-2 is a short version of the occurrence given by the injured who must have been under great pain and agony when he gave his statement a few minutes after his arrival at Malout hospital.
Whatever is contained therein is nothing but truth.
Intrinsically, the details given in P-16 show that all those details perhaps must no have been given by Khazan Singh himself.
But that in our views does not detract in the least from the veracity and truthfulness of the statement of the deceased contained in Exh. P-2.
We think that the High Court is not right in convicting the two appellants u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code with the aid of S. 34.
The only fact then remains that Chain Singh gave a spear blow near the chest of Khazan Singh.
The injury caused by this blow in the opinion of the doctor who held the postmortem examination on the dead body of Khazan Singh was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause his death.
holding: We hold that the occurrence did take place in the manner as found by the High Court.
Both the appellants took part in the occurrence.
But we think that the High Court is not right in convicting the two appellants u/s. 302 of the Indian Penal Code with the aid of S. 34.
Appellant Chain Singh was guilty of causing the death of Khazan Singh by giving the fatal blow with this spear on his chest.
In the result, we dismiss the appeal of appellant Chain Singh subject to changing his conviction from one under Section 302, read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code to one u/s. 302 simpliciter.

We allow the appeal of appellant Surat Singh in part, set aside his conviction and sentence under Section 302, read with S. 34 of the Indian Penal Code and instead convict him u/s. 324 of the Indian Penal Code.
